subject.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch

question: Should authenticated plugin runtimes be categorically denied from patching legacy ownerless session rows, even when that breaks previously working plugin cleanup or metadata workflows?
rationale: No stored owner exists to authorize safely, so preserving access weakens the isolation fix, while failing closed is an upgrade-visible behavior change that repository policy requires maintainers to own explicitly.

options.title: Approve fail-closed legacy rows
options.body: Reject plugin-runtime patches to ownerless rows, document the operator or non-plugin recovery path, and require upgrade proof before merge.

options.title: Add a trusted migration
options.body: Define a doctor or migration rule that assigns ownership only when a reliable historical authority can be proven, then reject remaining ownerless rows.

options.title: Preserve legacy access
options.body: Allow plugin runtimes to patch ownerless rows for compatibility, accepting that the ownership boundary remains weaker for legacy state.

recommendation.title: Approve fail-closed legacy rows
recommendation.body: Reject plugin-runtime patches to ownerless rows, document the operator or non-plugin recovery path, and require upgrade proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent session-store writer/accessor and compatibility history makes this the strongest available owner for the upgrade-sensitive authorization choice.
